phase3B.hypothesis: Temporary early liquidity relief reduces bootstrap insolvency without accelerating Fame.

candidates.description: Reduces applicable early-game daily obligations to 90 percent through day 15.
candidates.hypothesis: Lower recurring costs should prevent early insolvency without changing Fame efficiency.

candidates.description: Reduces applicable early-game daily obligations to 80 percent through day 15.
candidates.hypothesis: Lower recurring costs should prevent early insolvency without changing Fame efficiency.

candidates.description: Reduces applicable early-game daily obligations to 70 percent through day 15.
candidates.hypothesis: Lower recurring costs should prevent early insolvency without changing Fame efficiency.

candidates.description: Provides one emergency intervention of €250 through day 10 below €100.
candidates.hypothesis: A one-shot liquidity backstop should recover endangered runs without broadly enriching solvent runs.

candidates.description: Provides one emergency intervention of €500 through day 10 below €100.
candidates.hypothesis: A one-shot liquidity backstop should recover endangered runs without broadly enriching solvent runs.

candidates.description: Provides one emergency intervention of €750 through day 10 below €100.

candidates.description: Scales obligations to 60 percent through day 5 and 80 percent through day 10.
candidates.hypothesis: A tapered ramp should protect the opening while restoring full costs quickly.

candidates.description: Scales obligations to 75 percent through day 7.
candidates.hypothesis: A short moderate ramp should reduce opening failures with little surplus.

candidates.description: Scales obligations to 85 percent through day 10.

candidates.description: Reduces recurring daily obligations to 50 percent through day 60.
candidates.hypothesis: A longer but still temporary taper should cover the observed delayed bootstrap failures without enriching successful runs.

phase3C.hypothesis: A bounded dense-tour trade-off reduces late compounding while preserving early viability.

candidates.description: Applies 5 percent regional repeat-demand loss per gig, capped at 15 percent.
candidates.hypothesis: Expiring regional saturation should target dense schedules more than paced touring.

candidates.description: Applies 5 percent regional repeat-demand loss per gig, capped at 20 percent.
candidates.hypothesis: Expiring regional saturation should target dense schedules more than paced touring.

candidates.description: Applies 7.5 percent regional repeat-demand loss per gig, capped at 25 percent.
candidates.hypothesis: Expiring regional saturation should target dense schedules more than paced touring.

candidates.description: Applies 10 percent regional repeat-demand loss per gig over ten days, capped at 40 percent.
candidates.hypothesis: A broader expiring window should make dense regional routing carry delayed demand costs while preserving early cash.

candidates.description: Applies 10 percent regional repeat-demand loss per gig over eight days, capped at 40 percent.
candidates.hypothesis: A shorter saturation window should retain the late-game reduction while keeping day-20 money within its guardrail.

candidates.description: Applies 10 percent regional repeat-demand loss over eight days after day 20, capped at 40 percent.
candidates.hypothesis: Deferring saturation until after the bootstrap horizon should preserve day-20 cash while flattening later compounding.

candidates.description: Applies 12 percent regional repeat-demand loss over ten days after day 20, capped at 45 percent.
candidates.hypothesis: A stronger deferred saturation candidate tests whether P90 can be reduced without early damage.

candidates.description: Applies 1 harmony loss on consecutive gig days.
candidates.hypothesis: Dense touring stress should create a visible pacing trade-off.

candidates.description: Applies 2 harmony loss on consecutive gig days.
candidates.hypothesis: Dense touring stress should create a visible pacing trade-off.

candidates.description: Applies one harmony loss and ten percent lower recovery after consecutive gigs.
candidates.hypothesis: Combining small stress and recovery pressure may discourage density without a large cash penalty.
